title: Three Days and One Short Bank
subtitle: 灾害防范 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 灾害防范（人与自然·灾害防范·洪水与自救）
meta: 主题语境：灾害防范（人与自然·灾害防范·洪水与自救）　|　核心词汇：flood　|　正文 340 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flood 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1972 my grandfather ① survived a flood that no neighbour in the valley would have forgotten, and he said the surviving was the whole of the week. The ② flood, meaning the water itself and not the rain, ran three days and stayed unrecorded in the book; a flood, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ flood in that valley had the same short bank beside it, and the ④ flood at the far bend, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A flood, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; my grandfather said the recording is the part that fills three days.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flood was the whole of the matter, meaning the stream and not the water. The ⑥ flood, meaning the stream and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; flood, he said, is either something you survive or the only word that means both water and a stream. He said the stream is the part they remember.

By 1979 the ⑦ flood had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short bank. The ⑧ flood of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in July, was one valley and three days of recording; flood, he said, is either the one at the far bend or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flood I remember is the one recorded in the plan, which closed in 1981 and is still described as the quietest in the valley. A ⑩ flood, my mother said in 1983, is the only one that improves by being recorded; every flood, she said, is a stream that has agreed to look like water. She said the stream was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 洪水；水灾（指山谷里每一场旁边的那一场）
B. n. 洪水（指那一场本身，与降雨相对）
C. 固定搭配：survive a flood 熬过一场洪水
D. n. 洪水（指留给孩子们的那一场）
E. n. 洪水（抽象总称，指一个山谷的洪水之事）
F. n. 洪水（指计划里写到、被记录过的那一场）
G. n. 大量；大批（a flood of，指一件事里人人都等却无人记录的那样东西）
H. n. 大量（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人记录的那样东西）

items.q: survived a flood that no neighbour in the valley would have forgotten
The flood, meaning the water itself and not the rain
the flood at the far bend
the flood was the whole of the matter
the flood had become a line in a plan
The flood of the whole thing
A flood, my mother said in 1983

answers.why: survive a flood 意为“熬过一场洪水”，1972 年祖父熬过了一场山谷里没有一位邻居肯忘记的洪水。
flood 意为“洪水”，指那一场本身而不是降雨，它经过了三天而在簿子上没有被记录。
flood 意为“洪水”，指山谷里每一场旁边的那一场，每一场旁边都有同一道矮矮的河岸。
flood 意为“洪水”，指留给孩子们的那一场，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flood 意为“大量、大批”，指一件事里人人都等却无人记录的那样东西，叔叔说这一大批就是那件事的全部。
flood 意为“大量”，指人人都等却无人记录的那样东西而不是那一场洪水，是事情里人人都等、却无人记录的东西。
flood 意为“洪水”，指计划里写到、被记录过的那一场，到 1979 年这一场成了计划里的一行。
flood 意为“洪水”，祖父七月写道，整件事的洪水之事是一个山谷和三天的记录。
flood 意为“洪水”，我记得的是计划里记录过的那一场，1981 年结束了，至今仍被说成山谷里最安静的一场。
flood 为抽象总称，母亲 1983 年说，一场洪水是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的东西。
